extra_quotes: We investigate phonon scattering by oxygen-related defects using pretrained universal machine-learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs), molecular dynamics (MD), and phonon Boltzmann transport calculations.
The lattice thermal conductivity is calculated by iteratively solving the linearized phonon BTE [30] using a modified ShengBTE package [31].
In the SED approach, the defect scattering rate is estimated from the excess spectral linewidth of the defective supercell relative to the pristine supercell in MD simulations.
At high concentrations, however, the scattering rate deviates from linear scaling with oxygen content, suggesting limitations of independent-defect and pristine-phonon descriptions.

Although SED spectra can still be evaluated for highly disordered crystalline systems, extracting well-defined phonon lifetimes becomes increasingly challenging as mode mixing and spectral broadening obscure individual phonon peaks.
